hindi: अब इसके बाद हम भेषज के कल्प की व्याख्या करेंगे।
english: Now, therefore, we shall explain the preparation (kalpa) of medicines (bheṣaja).
notes: Opening formula of the chapter. 'kalpa' is rendered 'preparation'; the chapter goes on to land, collection, storage and the five forms of preparation.

words.gloss: according to the season, in due time
cold (śiśira); sunshine; wind; water; frequented by
cremation ground; shrine (caitya); deity; abode, temple; house; assembly hall
words.gram: dvandva; ends in the printed visarga form sabhāḥ, as printed; construction with virahite unclear

words.gloss: garden; anthill; saline soil; devoid of
kuśa grass (Desmostachya bipinnata; standard); rohiṣa grass (a fragrant grass, probably Cymbopogon; disputed); spread, covered
unctuous; black; golden; colour; sweet; fragrant; with soil
unclear; probably 'gently' or 'with clay' (printed form kept)

hindi: जांगल यानी रूखे खुले प्रदेश में, या साधारण प्रदेश में, ऋतु के अनुसार, शीत, धूप, वायु और जल से सेवित, समतल, शुद्ध, दाहिनी ओर जल बहने वाली, श्मशान, चैत्य, देवमन्दिर, घर और सभा से तथा बाग, दीमक की बांबी और ऊषर भूमि से रहित, कुश और रोहिष यानी सम्भवतः रूसा घास से ढकी, चिकनी, काली, सोने के रंग की, मीठी और सुगन्धित मिट्टी वाली, मुद्रित मृदावफाल अस्पष्ट है, अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार हल से जोती हुई, दूसरे अधिक बलवान वृक्षों से अनुपहत भूमि में औषध प्रशस्त माने जाते हैं। यह सामान्य रूप से भूमि की परीक्षा है।
english: In a jāṅgala (dry, open country) or in a common region, according to the season, in land that is frequented by cold, sunshine, wind and water, level, clean, with water flowing to the right, free from cremation ground, shrine (caitya), temple, house and assembly hall, and from garden, anthill and saline soil, spread with kuśa grass (Desmostachya bipinnata) and rohiṣa grass (probably a fragrant Cymbopogon grass; disputed), with soil that is unctuous, black, golden-coloured, sweet and fragrant, ploughed (the printed 'mṛdāvaphāla' is unclear; on a conjectural reading, with a ploughshare), and not harmed by other, stronger trees: medicines are praised. Thus it is the general examination of land.

text_flags.why: possible: 'caā' leaves an uncontracted hiatus; sandhi would give 'cā'
possible: 'muttikā' is not a word; 'mṛttikā' (soil) fits the sense and the list of qualities
the opening 'mṛdāvaphāla-' is not a clear word; possibly 'mṛdu' + 'avaphāla' or 'mṛdā' (with clay); no firm correction offered
possible: the print joins praśasyante and iti with an ai junction that sandhi does not give; read as the verb praśasyante plus iti

notes: Long single sentence; the locatives (jāṅgale ... bhūmau) all describe the land, and the verb is 'praśasyante' at the end ('are praised'). 'jāṅgala' is a technical term for dry, sparsely watered, open country (standard). kuśa = Desmostachya bipinnata (standard); rohiṣa = a fragrant grass, probably Cymbopogon (lemongrass type); disputed. 'mṛdāvaphālakṛṣṭe' is doubtful: the words kept are 'mṛdā' (probably gently, or with clay) and 'avaphāla' (unclear), 'ploughed' (kṛṣṭa) is sure; the reading is conjectural. 'sevite': 'frequented by' is taken literally. 'pradakṣiṇodaka' is taken as water flowing to the right (clockwise). 'sabhāścaārāma' shows a hiatus typo (see text_flags). 'iti' closes the statement ('thus ... general examination of land').
lines_deva: जांगले साधारणे वा देशे यथाकालं शिशिरातपपवनसलिलसेविते समे शुचौ प्रदक्षिणोदके श्मशानचैत्यदेवतायतनागारसभाश्चआरामवल्मीकोषरविरहिते कुशरोहिषास्तीर्णे स्निग्धकृष्णसुवर्णवर्णमधुरसुरभिमुत्तिके मृदावफालकृष्टेऽनुपहतेऽन्यैर्बलवत्तरैर्द्रुमैर्भेषजानि प्रशस्यंतइति सामान्यतो भूमिपरीक्षा
lines_iast: jāṃgale sādhāraṇe vā deśe yathākālaṃ śiśirātapapavanasalilasevite same śucau pradakṣiṇodake śmaśānacaityadevatāyatanāgārasabhāścaārāmavalmīkoṣaravirahite kuśarohiṣāstīrṇe snigdhakṛṣṇasuvarṇavarṇamadhurasurabhimuttike mṛdāvaphālakṛṣṭe'nupahate'nyairbalavattarairdrumairbheṣajāni praśasyaṃtaiti sāmānyato bhūmiparīkṣā

hindi: विशेष रूप से पथरीली, स्थिर, भारी, श्याम, पतली और मोटी घास वाली, अधिकतर वृक्षों और सस्य वाली, अपने गुण की प्रचुरता वाली।
english: In particular: stony, firm, heavy, dark, with thin and thick grass, mostly with trees and crops (sasya), abounding in its own quality.
notes: The feminine adjectives agree with 'bhūmi' (land) understood from 2; no verb. 'svaguṇa' is 'its own quality'; the text does not name the element here, but the following units name the water, fire, wind and space types, so this is probably the earth type (inferred, not stated). 'kṛśasthūlatṛṇā' = 'with thin and thick grass' taken literally.
lines_deva: विशेषतस्त्वश्मवती स्थिरा गुर्वी श्यामा कृशस्थूलतृणा वृक्षसस्यप्राया स्वगुणभूयिष्ठा
lines_iast: viśeṣatastvaśmavatī sthirā gurvī śyāmā kṛśasthūlatṛṇā vṛkṣasasyaprāyā svaguṇabhūyiṣṭhā

words.gloss: unctuous; grass; crops (sasya); tender; (word continues in the next token)
words.gram: bahuvrīhi, compound (broken by a space in print)

hindi: चिकनी, शीतल, पास में जल वाली, चिकनी घास, सस्य और कोमल पत्तों से भरपूर, श्वेत और जल के गुण की प्रचुरता वाली।
english: Unctuous, cool, with water near, mostly with unctuous grass, crops (sasya) and tender leaves, white, and abounding in the quality of water.

text_flags.why: possible: 'āsañja' does not suit 'water'; 'āsanna' (near) fits
a stray space splits 'komala' in print
possible: 'aṃgu' is not a word; 'ambu' (water) fits the series of earth, water, fire, wind, space types (see units 5 to 7 and 8)

notes: Feminine adjectives agree with 'bhūmi' understood. The type is presumably the water type (the quality is 'ambu' on the suggested reading); inferred. 'āsañjodakā' read as 'āsanna-udakā' (conjectural, see flag). The word 'komala' is split by a space in the print: the first token 'koma' and the second 'ladalaprāyā'. In the word list the broken word is shown joined with a trailing hyphen.
lines_deva: स्निग्धा शीतलाऽऽसञ्जोदका स्निग्धतृणसस्यकोम लदलप्राया शुक्ला चांगुगुणभूयिष्ठा
lines_iast: snigdhā śītalā''sañjodakā snigdhatṛṇasasyakoma ladalaprāyā śuklā cāṃguguṇabhūyiṣṭhā

hindi: अनेक रंगों वाली, हल्के फूलों वाली, बहुत विरल पाण्डु वृक्षों की वृद्धि वाली और अग्नि के गुण की प्रचुरता वाली।
english: Of various colours, having light flowers, with a very sparse growth of pale trees, and abounding in the quality of fire.
notes: Feminine adjectives agree with 'bhūmi' understood. 'pāṇḍu' is 'pale' (not 'yellow'). The type is the fire type ('agniguṇa'). 'laghupuṣpavatī' could be 'having small flowers' or 'light flowers'; the literal 'light' is kept.

words.gloss: thin, slight; hollow; saline soil; mostly

hindi: गधे और राख के रंग की, रूखी, अधिकतर तनु, कोटर और ऊषर वाली, थोड़े रस वाली वृद्धि से युक्त और वायु के गुण की प्रचुरता वाली।
english: Of the colour of a donkey and of ash, dry, mostly slight, hollow and saline, with a growth of little taste (rasa), and abounding in the quality of wind.
notes: Feminine adjectives agree with 'bhūmi' understood. 'rāsabhabhasmavarṇā' is read as 'colour of donkey and ash'. 'tanukoṭaroṣara' is read as three members (tanu, koṭara, ūṣara); the grouping (e.g. 'thin hollows') is uncertain. 'alparasaprarohā' = 'growth of little rasa (taste, sap)'. Wind type ('anilaguṇa').

hindi: कोमल, समतल, गड्ढों वाली, अस्पष्ट रस वाले जल से युक्त, किनारों पर बड़े वृक्षों वाली, श्याम और आकाश के गुण की प्रचुरता वाली।
english: Soft, level, having pits, with water of indistinct taste (rasa), with great trees at its edges, dark, and abounding in the quality of space (ākāśa).

text_flags.why: possible: feminine of mṛdu is 'mṛdvī'
possible: 'śvaara' is not a word; 'śvabhra' (pit, hollow) fits the print shape and the sense

notes: Feminine adjectives agree with 'bhūmi' understood. Space type ('ākāśaguṇa'). 'śvabhravatī' is a conjectural reading (see flag). 'mahāparyantavṛkṣā' is read 'with great trees at the boundary'; 'paryanta' could also mean 'ending in' (ambiguous).

hindi: उनमें जल और पृथ्वी के गुणों की प्रचुरता वाली भूमियों में उत्पन्न हुए, विरेचन और बृंहण यानी पुष्टिकारक प्रशस्त माने जाते हैं।
english: Among these, (ones) born in lands abounding in the qualities of water and earth are praised as purgative (virecana) and nourishing (bṛṃhaṇa).
notes: The subject 'jātāni' is a bare neuter plural 'born (ones)', that is the medicines of unit 2; the noun is not stated. 'virecana' = purgation, taken as predicate adjectives. Earth and water types correspond to the types of units 3 and 4 (inferred, not stated).
lines_deva: तत्रांबुपृथिवीगुणभूयिष्ठासु भूमिषु जातानि विरेचनानि बृंहणानि च शस्यंते
lines_iast: tatrāṃbupṛthivīguṇabhūyiṣṭhāsu bhūmiṣu jātāni virecanāni bṛṃhaṇāni ca śasyaṃte

words.gloss: fire; wind; space; quality; most abundant

hindi: अग्नि, वायु और आकाश के गुणों की प्रचुरता वाली भूमियों में वमन के।
english: In (lands) abounding in the qualities of fire, wind and space: (ones) for vomiting (vamana).
notes: Elliptical: 'jātāni' and 'praśasyante' carry over from unit 8; no verb is supplied in the translation. 'bhūmiṣu' (lands) is understood from 8.

hindi: सब गुणों से युक्त भूमियों में उभयतोभाग यानी दोनों ओर भाग वाले।
english: In (lands) endowed with all the qualities: both-way (ubhayatobhāga) ones.
notes: Elliptical (from 8 and 9). 'ubhayatobhāga' is a technical term, literally 'having a share on both sides'; it is commonly understood as acting both upward and downward (emetic and purgative); probable, not stated in the line. The 'both-way' rendering is kept literal.

hindi: आकाश के गुण की प्रचुरता वाली भूमियों में शमन करने वाले।
english: In (lands) abounding in the quality of space (ākāśa): pacifying (śamana) ones.
notes: Elliptical (verb and 'jātāni' from 8). 'śamana' = pacifying, palliative (not purgative or emetic).

hindi: इस प्रकार वे अत्यन्त बलवान होते हैं।
english: Thus (they) become the most powerful.
notes: The subject is the medicines (neuter plural), understood. 'balavattama' is the superlative of 'balavat'.

words.gloss: born in due time, in season
attained; complete; measure; taste (rasa); potency (vīrya); smell
time; sunshine; mi (unclear, printed form kept); water; wind; weapons; creatures
not harmed; smell; colour; taste (rasa); touch; potency (prabhāva)
in the northern (the first letter 'u' stands at the end of the previous token)

hindi: उनमें जो काल में उत्पन्न हुए हैं, जिन्होंने पूर्ण मात्रा, रस, वीर्य और गन्ध पा ली है, जो काल, धूप, अस्पष्ट मुद्रित मि, जल, वायु, शस्त्र और जन्तुओं से गन्ध, वर्ण, रस, स्पर्श और प्रभाव में अनुपहत हैं, जिनकी जड़ें गहरी हैं और जो उत्तर दिशा में स्थित हैं।
english: Among these, those which are born in their time, have attained full measure, taste (rasa), potency (vīrya) and smell, whose smell, colour, taste, touch and potency (prabhāva) have not been harmed by time, sunshine, mi (unclear), water, wind, weapons and creatures, whose roots are deep, and which stand in the northern direction.

text_flags.why: possible: 'mi' (printed) is not a word here; 'agni' (fire) is a conjecture only
possible: 'm' for 'n': 'prabhāvāny' (n. pl.) agrees with 'anupahata ... prabhāvāni'
the first letter 'u' is attached to the previous token 'mūlānyu'; the word is 'udīcyām'

notes: The relative clause 'yāni ... sthitāni' continues into unit 14 ('teṣām'). The word 'mi' in the long compound is unclear; 'agni' is only a possible conjecture, so the list is rendered 'mi (unclear)'. The print splits 'udīcyām' as 'mūlānyu | dīcyāṃ'; the second token carries the words 'dīcyām'. The first token ends with the letter 'u' of 'udīcyām'; the second token carries the word. 'upagata-sampūrṇa-pramāṇa': 'attained complete measure'. 'prabhāva' = specific potency, kept.
lines_deva: तत्र यानि कालजान्युपगतसंपूर्णप्रमाणरसवीर्यगंधानि कालातपमिसलिलपवनशस्त्रजंतुभिरनुपहतगंधवर्णरसस्पर्शप्रभावाम्यवगाढमूलान्यु दीच्यां दिशि स्थितानि

words.gloss: to be taken, to be gathered

hindi: उनमें से, हाल में उगी हुई शाखा और पत्ता वर्षा और वसन्त में ग्रहण करने योग्य है।
english: Of these, the branch and leaf (śākhā, palāśa), recently grown, are to be taken in the rainy season and in spring.
notes: 'palāśa' is taken as 'leaf'. The singular neuter dvandva 'śākhāpalāśam' is read as 'branch and leaf' (collective). The relative clause of unit 13 appears to complete here.

hindi: ग्रीष्म में जड़ें, या शिशिर में जिनके पत्ते झड़ चुके और उग आए हैं उनके।
english: In summer, the roots; or in the cold season (śiśira), of those whose leaves have fallen and sprouted.
notes: Elliptical: 'grāhyāṇi' (to be taken) carried over from 14. 'śīrṇaprarūḍhaparṇānām' is ambiguous (those whose leaves are fallen and grown again, or whose fallen leaves have been replaced); the literal rendering is kept. Subject of the genitive is left open in the Sanskrit.

words.gloss: bark; tuber, bulb (kanda); milk, milky sap (kṣīra)

hindi: शरद में छाल, कन्द और क्षीर यानी दूध।
english: In autumn: bark, tuber (kanda) and milk (kṣīra).
notes: Elliptical ('grāhyāṇi' carried). 'kṣīra' is 'milk'; in a plant context it probably means the milky latex of the plant (probable, not stated in the line).

hindi: हेमन्त में सार यानी सम्भवतः काठ का भीतरी भाग।
english: In winter (hemanta): the sāra (essence, core; probably heartwood).
notes: Elliptical ('grāhyāṇi' carried). 'sāra' = essence, core; 'heartwood' is the usual sense for a woody plant (probable).

hindi: ऋतु के अनुसार फल और फूल।
english: Fruit and flower according to the season.
notes: Elliptical ('grāhyam' carried). 'yathartu' is read as 'yathā ṛtu'.

hindi: दूसरे फिर कहते हैं।
english: Others, again, say:
notes: Introduces the next view (unit 20). 'punar' is here 'again' as an introducing particle ('however'); the line leaves the content to the next unit.

hindi: सौम्य औषध सौम्य ऋतुओं में, आग्नेय आग्नेयों में।
english: Saumya (gentle) medicines (auṣadha) in the saumya seasons, āgneya (fiery) ones in the āgneya (ones).
notes: Elliptical: 'grāhyāṇi' (to be taken) carried over. The text does not name which seasons are saumya or āgneya, so none is named here. 'auṣadha' (medicine) is the printed form.

hindi: इस प्रकार वे अविकृत और अधिक पूर्ण रस और वीर्य वाले होते हैं।
english: Thus (they) become unspoiled, with fuller taste (rasa) and potency (vīrya).
notes: 'āpūrṇatara' is a comparative: 'fuller'. 'avyāpanna' = not spoiled, not damaged. Subject (the herbs) understood.

hindi: तब मंगल आचार और कल्याणकारी वृत्ति वाला, शुद्ध, श्वेत वस्त्र पहने हुए, देवता, दोनों अश्विनी कुमारों, गौओं और ब्राह्मणों की पूजा करके, उपवास किए हुए, पूर्वमुख या उत्तरमुख होकर ग्रहण करे।
english: Then, of auspicious conduct and good behaviour, clean, in white clothes, having worshipped the deity, the two Aśvins, cows and brahmins, having fasted, facing east or facing north, he should take (it).

text_flags.why: possible: the print runs the two words together without a space; the expected form is the hiatus prāṅmukha udaṅmukho (aḥ before a vowel other than a drops the visarga)

notes: The object of 'gṛhṇīyāt' is not stated (the medicines of the previous units). 'devatām aśvinau' may be two separate objects (the deity; the two Aśvins) or an apposition ('the deity, the two Aśvins'); the first is rendered. 'maṅgalācārakalyāṇavṛtti': 'one whose conduct is auspicious and whose way of life is good'.
lines_deva: अथ मंगलाचारकल्याणवृत्तिः शुचिः शुक्लवासाः संपूज्य देवतामश्विनौ गोब्राह्मणांश्च कृतोपवासः प्राङ्मुखउदङ्मुखो वा गृह्णीयात्
lines_iast: atha maṃgalācārakalyāṇavṛttiḥ śuciḥ śuklavāsāḥ saṃpūjya devatāmaśvinau gobrāhmaṇāṃśca kṛtopavāsaḥ prāṅmukhaudaṅmukho vā gṛhṇīyāt

words.gloss: suitable; having good quality; in a vessel
fire; water; steam, moisture (upasveda); smoke; dust; mouse; quadruped; and so on; not to be approached
unclear (printed form kept; possibly 'under one's own control')

hindi: और ग्रहण करके, अनुरूप गुण वाले पात्र में रखकर, पूर्व और उत्तर द्वार वाले घरों में, एक भाग में वायुरहित और वायुयुक्त स्थानों में, नित्य पुष्प, उपहार और बलिकर्म वाले स्थानों में, अग्नि, जल, भाप, धुएँ, धूल, चूहों, चौपायों आदि से अगम्य, स्ववश्यानि अस्पष्ट शब्द जिसे अनुमान से अपने वश में पढ़ा गया है, शिक्यों में लटकाकर रखे।
english: And having taken (them) and stored (them) in a vessel of suitable, good quality, he should keep them hung in slings (śikya) in houses with east and north doors, in places of one part windless and breezy, in places of constant flower-offering and bali rites, (them) not to be approached by fire, water, steam (upasveda), smoke, dust, mice, quadrupeds and so on, svavaśyāni (unclear; on a conjectural reading, under one's own control).

text_flags.why: the word is not clear; sva-vaśyāni (own-controlled) is only a conjecture and no correction is offered

notes: Very dense sentence; the structure is a chain of locatives with an absolutive and the final verb 'sthāpayet'. 'nivātapravātaikadeśeṣu' is uncertain ('in places of one part windless and breezy'); the grouping of 'eka' is conjectural. 'pūrvottaradvāreṣu' = 'with east and north doors' (literal; whether 'east or north' is not decided). 'svavaśyāni' is unclear: 'sva-vaśyāni' (own-controlled) is only a conjecture and the translation says so. 'upasveda' = steam or moisture. The object (the gathered medicines) is understood, not stated.
lines_deva: गृहीत्वा चानुरूपगुणवद्भाजने संस्थाप्यागारेषु पूर्वोत्तरद्वारेषु निवातप्रवातैकदेशेषु नित्यपुष्पोपहारबलिकर्मस्वग्निसलिलोपस्वेदधूमरजोमूषिकचतुष्पादाद्यनभिगमनीयानि स्ववश्यानि शिक्येष्वासज्य स्थापयेत्
lines_iast: gṛhītvā cānurūpaguṇavadbhājane saṃsthāpyāgāreṣu pūrvottaradvāreṣu nivātapravātaikadeśeṣu nityapuṣpopahārabalikarmasvagnisalilopasvedadhūmarajomūṣikacatuṣpādādyanabhigamanīyāni svavaśyāni śikyeṣvāsajya sthāpayet

hindi: वे जो क्षीर सहित हैं, उन्हें तैयार करे।
english: He should prepare those (that are) with milk (sakṣīra).

text_flags.why: possible: the print has short a in sakṣīraṇy; the neuter plural sakṣīrāṇi needs ā

notes: 'sakṣīra' is 'with milk' (or 'with milky sap'); whether it means milky plants or 'together with milk' is not decided by the line. 'upakalpayet' = 'should prepare, arrange'. The Hindi 'क्षीर वाले बनाकर' is avoided; the Hindi keeps the plain sense.

hindi: तदंमत्ताव अस्पष्ट शब्द; अनुमान से, जिनका वर्ष बीता नहीं है वे।
english: tadaṃmattāva (unclear); on a conjectural reading, (ones) whose year has not passed.

text_flags.why: the initial part 'tadaṃmattāva' is not a recognisable word; the end 'anatikrānta-saṃvatsarāṇi' (those whose year has not passed) looks sound, but the junction is uncertain

notes: Damaged or garbled word; only the end 'natikrāṃtasaṃvatsarāṇi' is read ('whose year has not passed'). Unit 26 begins 'purāṇāni tu', 'but old (ones)', which suggests that 25 speaks of drugs not yet a year old; that is inferred, not stated. The negation in 'natikrānta' depends on the damaged junction before it (tāva-n-atikrānta); the opposite sense 'whose year has passed' is not excluded by the print alone. The contrast of unit 26 ('purāṇāni tu') supports the negated reading.

words.gloss: pippalī (long pepper, Piper longum; standard); viḍaṅga (Embelia ribes, false black pepper; standard); jaggery (guḍa); honey (madhu); ghee (ghṛta)

hindi: परन्तु पुराने: पिप्पली यानी पीपर, विडंग यानी वायविडंग, गुड़, शहद और घी।
english: But old (ones): pippalī (long pepper), viḍaṅga (false black pepper; Embelia ribes), jaggery (guḍa), honey (madhu) and ghee (ghṛta).
notes: Identifications: pippalī = Piper longum (standard); viḍaṅga = Embelia ribes (standard; some also use Embelia tsjeriam-cottam). 'purāṇāni' is taken to qualify the listed items. Elliptical: no verb stated.

hindi: और भी।
english: And further:
notes: Introduces a further list (units 28 and 29).

words.gloss: unclear (printed form kept; possibly related to vaṣkayaṇī, a cow with a grown calf; uncertain)

hindi: बौष्क्यण अस्पष्ट शब्द वाला दूध ग्रहण करना चाहिए, तथा मल और मूत्र नीरोग।
english: Milk (bauṣkyaṇa, unclear) is to be taken, and dung and urine, disease-free (nīruja).

text_flags.why: possible: 'śakṛn-mūtra' (dung and urine) is the regular form; 'śakan' lacks the 'ṛ'

notes: 'bauṣkyaṇa' is unclear; it may relate to 'vaṣkayaṇī' (a cow with a grown calf), but that is a guess, so the word is left untranslated. 'nīrujam' (disease-free) is neuter singular and presumably refers to the animal source; not stated. The animal is not named in the line. The collective neuter 'śakṛnmūtram' is taken as 'dung and urine'.
lines_deva: क्षीरं बौष्क्यणं ग्राह्यं शकन्मूत्रं च नीरुजं
lines_iast: kṣīraṃ bauṣkyaṇaṃ grāhyaṃ śakanmūtraṃ ca nīrujaṃ

words.gloss: dhātu (tissue, constituent); tail; horn; (word continues in the next token)

hindi: आयु और बल वालों के धातु, पूँछ, सींग, खुर आदि, अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार।
english: Of (those) possessing age and strength: dhātu, tail, horn, hoof and so on, on a conjectural reading.

text_flags.why: possible: the word is broken by a space and garbled ('śrṛṃ ga-ra'); 'śṛṅga-khura' (horn, hoof) fits the sense

notes: The nouns are not stated; presumably animal products (the previous unit speaks of milk, dung, urine), but this is inferred. 'vayobalavatām' is 'of those having age and strength' (presumably of suitable age and strength; not stated). 'dhātu' is left as 'dhātu' (tissue or constituent; the sense here is unclear). The extra 'ra' in 'garakhura' is unexplained.

hindi: औषधों का काढ़ा पाँच प्रकार का बनाना चाहिए।
english: A fivefold decoction (kaṣāya) of medicines is to be prepared.
notes: 'kaṣāya' here is a preparation (decoction) and not the astringent taste; the five forms named in 31 are juice, paste, decoction, cold infusion and hot infusion, so 'kaṣāya' is used generally for a preparation of the medicine.

words.gloss: expressed juice (niryāsa; defined in 33 as svarasa)

hindi: निर्यास यानी स्वरस, कल्क, निर्यूह यानी काढ़ा, शीत और फाण्ट।
english: Niryāsa (expressed juice), kalka (paste), niryūha (decoction), śīta (cold infusion) and phāṇṭa (hot infusion).

text_flags.why: possible: 'nirdhūha' is not a word; unit 37 prints 'niryūhaḥ'

notes: List of the five forms. In this chapter 'niryāsa' is the expressed juice (svarasa), as unit 33 defines it, not gum. 'śīta' and 'phāṇṭa' are defined in 42 and 43; the modern names 'cold infusion' and 'hot infusion' are interpretation (probable).

words.gloss: in the order of the preceding, according to precedence

hindi: वे पूर्व के क्रम से बलवान हैं।
english: They are strong in the order of precedence (yathāpūrvam).
notes: 'yathāpūrvam' = 'as before, in order of the preceding'; the usual sense is that each earlier one in the list of 31 is stronger, but the line does not say more. 'te' refers to the five forms of 31.

hindi: उनमें तत्काल उखाड़े, धोए, कुचले और कपड़े से निचोड़े हुए का जो स्वरस है, वह निर्यास है।
english: Among these, of (one) freshly pulled up, washed, crushed and pressed out through a cloth (tāntava), the own juice (svarasa) is niryāsa.
notes: The thing pulled up and pressed is a medicine, not named (genitive singular). 'tāntava' = of threads, a cloth; 'through a cloth' is the natural sense. This unit defines niryāsa as svarasa (expressed juice).
lines_deva: तत्र सद्यः समुद्धृतप्रक्षालितक्षुण्णस्य तांतवनिष्पीडितस्य स्वरसो निर्यासः
lines_iast: tatra sadyaḥ samuddhṛtaprakṣālitakṣuṇṇasya tāṃtavaniṣpīḍitasya svaraso niryāsaḥ

words.gloss: stone; tooth; and so on; ground

hindi: पत्थर, दाँत आदि से पीसा हुआ कल्क है।
english: But (that) ground with a stone, teeth and so on is kalka (paste).
notes: The ground thing is a medicine, not stated. 'upala' = grinding stone, 'daśana' = tooth. 'ādi' is rendered 'and so on'.

words.gloss: fine; of cloth; fallen, passed through; powder

hindi: बारीक कपड़े से छनकर गिरा हुआ चूर्ण।
english: A powder that has fallen through a fine cloth.
notes: Elliptical: no verb and no stated subject. The line gives a powder (cūrṇa) sifted through a fine cloth; whether it defines a sixth item or continues the kalka of 34 is not decided by the line, and unit 36 compares 'its' difference from kalka. 'cyuta' = fallen, dropped (through).

hindi: उसका, सम्पूर्ण द्रव्य के न छोड़े जाने से और शीघ्र उपयोग से, कल्क से भेद नहीं है।
english: Of that, because the whole substance is not abandoned and because of quick use, there is no difference from kalka.

text_flags.why: a space separates samasta from dravya- in print; read as one compound

notes: 'tasya' refers to the powder of 35 (inferred). 'samasta dravya' are separate tokens in print; read 'samasta-dravya-aparityāgāt' (non-abandonment of the whole substance). 'āśutopayoga' = 'āśutā' (quickness) + 'upayoga' (use).

hindi: क्वाथ यानी काढ़ा निर्यूह है।
english: Kvātha (decoction) is niryūha.
notes: Gives kvātha as another name for niryūha; both are rendered 'decoction'. Elliptical: no verb.

words.gloss: copper; iron; earthen; any one of; in a pot
unclear (printed form kept; possibly ākalayya, 'having reckoned')

hindi: वह निर्यूह: विदारने योग्य औषधियों को बारीक विदारकर, काटने योग्य को कटवाकर, जल से धोकर, शुद्ध, रूखे और नीचे से लिपे हुए ताँबे, लोहे या मिट्टी में से किसी एक बर्तन में डालकर, बहुत जल ग्रहण कराई गई औषधियों का आकलथ्य, यह शब्द अस्पष्ट है, अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार अनुमान लगाकर, जितने जल से रस छूटने की अवस्था हो, उतना जल डाले और सुखाए।
english: As for that (niryūha): having split finely the herbs that are to be split, having cut those that are to be cut, having washed them with water, having put them into a pot that is clean, dry and smeared below, any one of copper, iron or clay, and, of the herbs made to take abundant water, ākalathya (unclear; on a conjectural reading, having reckoned), he should pour in as much water as makes a state of released taste (rasa), and should reduce it.

text_flags.why: possible: 'rūkṣa' (dry) has a long ū
possible: ākalathya is not a word; ākalayya (having reckoned, estimated) is a conjecture; th and y are close in the Devanagari print

notes: Dense preparation of the niryūha (decoction). 'sa tu' may mean 'he, however' (the physician) or 'that (niryūha)'. 'ākalathya' is an unclear word: perhaps a typo for 'ākalayya' (having reckoned, estimated), conjectural; the translation marks it. 'bahulapānīyagrāhitānām' is read as 'of those made to take abundant water'. 'adhaḥpraliptāyām' = smeared below (the pot). 'śoṣayet' is rendered 'reduce' (literally 'dry up').
lines_deva: स तु भेद्यान्यौषधान्यणुशो भेदयित्वा छेद्यानि च छेदयित्वा प्रक्षाल्योदकेन शुचौ रुक्षायामधःप्रलिप्तायां ताम्रायोमृन्मयान्यतमस्थाल्यां समावाप्य बहुलपानीयग्राहितानामौषधानामाकलथ्य यावता मुक्तरसता स्यात्तावदुदकमासेचयेच्छोषयेच्च
lines_iast: sa tu bhedyānyauṣadhānyaṇuśo bhedayitvā chedyāni ca chedayitvā prakṣālyodakena śucau rukṣāyāmadhaḥpraliptāyāṃ tāmrāyomṛnmayānyatamasthālyāṃ samāvāpya bahulapānīyagrāhitānāmauṣadhānāmākalathya yāvatā muktarasatā syāttāvadudakamāsecayecchoṣayecca

words.gram: pres. part. sam-upa-√gam, m. inst. sg.

hindi: तब आग पर रखकर, बड़े आसन पर सुख से बैठा हुआ, सब ओर से निरन्तर देखता हुआ और करछी से हिलाता हुआ, चारों ओर पहुँचती हुई मृदु आग से सिद्ध करे।
english: Then, having placed it on the fire, seated comfortably on a large seat, constantly watching from all sides and stirring with a ladle, he should prepare it with a gentle fire reaching all around.
notes: Continues 38; the object (the pot with the herbs and water) is understood. 'sādhayet' = 'should prepare' (cook). 'mahati āsane' = 'on a large seat'. 'darvī' = ladle or spoon.
lines_deva: अथाग्नावधिश्रित्य महत्यासने सुखोपविष्टः सर्वतः सततमवलोकयन् दर्व्या च विघट्टयन् मृदुना च परितः समुपगच्छता ऽनलेन साधयेत्
lines_iast: athāgnāvadhiśritya mahatyāsane sukhopaviṣṭaḥ sarvataḥ satatamavalokayan darvyā ca vighaṭṭayan mṛdunā ca paritaḥ samupagacchatā 'nalena sādhayet

hindi: और उतारकर, भली-भाँति छानकर, योग्य स्पर्श वाले को प्रयोग करे।
english: And having taken it down, well strained, of suitable touch, he should use (it).
notes: 'yathārhasparśam': literally 'of touch as is fitting'; whether this refers to the warmth is not stated, so the literal 'touch' is kept. The object is the decoction, understood.

words.gloss: milk; and so on; together with
well, fully; released; (word continues in the next token)
words.gram: compound (broken by a space in print)

hindi: और क्षीर आदि के साथ द्रव्य का रस भली-भाँति छूटा हुआ नहीं होता, इसलिए पहले जल का क्वाथ करके, उसके उपदेश के अनुसार न जलाते हुए क्षीर आदि के साथ क्वाथ करे।
english: And a substance together with milk and the like does not become one whose taste (rasa) is fully released; so, preceded by a decoction in water, he should boil it with milk and the like, as instructed, not scorched.

text_flags.why: possible: 'kvāth-' (to boil) is the usual form

notes: 'samyaṅmukta rasaṃ' is broken by a space in print and read as 'samyak-mukta-rasam'. 'tadupadeśānupadagdham' is uncertain: read as 'not scorched, according to that instruction'. The first half gives the reason ('iti', thus).
lines_deva: क्षीरादिसहितं च द्रव्यं न सम्यङ्मुक्त रसं भवतीति वारिक्वाथपूर्वकं क्षीराद्यैस्तदुपदेशानुपदग्धं काथयेत्
lines_iast: kṣīrādisahitaṃ ca dravyaṃ na samyaṅmukta rasaṃ bhavatīti vārikvāthapūrvakaṃ kṣīrādyaistadupadeśānupadagdhaṃ kāthayet

hindi: ठण्डे जल में भिगोया हुआ, रात भर रखा हुआ और छना हुआ शीत है।
english: But (that) soaked in cold water, kept overnight and strained is śīta (cold infusion).
notes: Defines śīta. The thing soaked is a medicine, not named. The modern name 'cold infusion' is interpretation (probable).

hindi: गरम जल में कुचला हुआ, भिगोया हुआ और छना हुआ फाण्ट है।
english: (That) crushed and soaked (abhisuta) in hot water and strained is phāṇṭa (hot infusion).

text_flags.why: possible: 'abhiṣuta' (steeped, pressed) is the regular form; the print has 's'

notes: Defines phāṇṭa. 'abhisuta' is read as 'steeped, soaked' (from abhi-√su, 'abhiṣuta'). The modern name 'hot infusion' is interpretation (probable).

words.gloss: well; taste (rasa); potency (vīrya); and so on
disease; patient; and so on; from the strength
unclear (printed form kept; possibly 'kalpanā' with a stray ending)

hindi: उनमें औषध के रस, वीर्य आदि को भली-भाँति देखकर तथा रोग, रोगी आदि के बल के अनुसार, निर्यास आदि के कल्प का, अनुमान से, क्योंकि पाठ अस्पष्ट है, और मात्रा का आश्रय ले।
english: Among these, having properly examined the taste (rasa), potency (vīrya) and so on of the medicine, and according to the strength of the disease, the patient and so on, he should resort to the preparation of niryāsa and the others (on a conjectural reading of 'kalpanāva nām') and to the dose (mātrā).

text_flags.why: possible: 'āturaādi' leaves a hiatus; sandhi gives 'āturādi'
the word is split by a space and not clear; 'kalpanā' with an unexplained ending 'va nām'

notes: The words 'kalpanāva' and 'nām' are split by a space and unclear; 'kalpanā' (preparation) is a conjecture only and the translation says so. 'mātrā' = dose. 'ādi' = 'and so on'. The sentence tells the physician to base the choice of form and dose on examination.
lines_deva: तत्र सम्यग्रसवीर्यादीन्यौषधस्य समीक्ष्य व्याध्यातुरआदिबलतश्च निर्यासादीनां कल्पनाव नां मात्रां च संश्रयेत्
lines_iast: tatra samyagrasavīryādīnyauṣadhasya samīkṣya vyādhyāturaādibalataśca niryāsādīnāṃ kalpanāva nāṃ mātrāṃ ca saṃśrayet

hindi: और ऐसा कुछ कहते हैं।
english: And thus some say:
notes: Introduces the quotation of units 46 and 47.

hindi: मात्रा की कोई निश्चित व्यवस्था नहीं है; शरीर, दोष, बल, आयु
english: There is no fixed rule for the dose (mātrā); the body, doṣa, strength, age

text_flags.why: possible: genitive 'mātrāyāḥ' needs the visarga
possible: anusvāra and 'na' transposed; 'vyavasthāna' (fixed rule) fits the sense

notes: The sentence continues in unit 47 (the accusatives are completed by 'ālocya'). Conjectural reading of 'mātrāyā na vyavasthāṃna' as 'mātrāyāḥ na vyavasthānam' (no fixed rule of dose); an alternative reading with 'na' twice cannot be excluded. Alternative reading of the second flag: 'vyavasthā na' (stray anusvāra) rather than 'vyavasthānam'; the print alone does not decide.
lines_deva: मात्राया न व्यवस्थांन देहं दोषं बलं वयः
lines_iast: mātrāyā na vyavasthāṃna dehaṃ doṣaṃ balaṃ vayaḥ

hindi: इन सबको और देश तथा काल को विचारकर औषध का प्रयोग करे।
english: Having considered (these) and place and time, he should administer the medicine (bhaiṣajya).
notes: Appears to complete the sentence of 46: 'having considered the body, doṣa, strength, age, and place and time, one should administer the medicine'. Taken together the saying is quoted from 'some' (45). 'avacārayet' = 'should administer, apply' (OPEN wording in the glossary).

hindi: इस प्रकार बस, पर्याप्त।
english: Thus, enough.
notes: A closing remark ending the quotation of 'some' and the discussion of dose; 'alam' = enough. Meaning slightly open.

hindi: वह इस प्रकार बुद्धिमानों के ज्ञान के प्रबोध के लिए उपदिष्ट है।
english: That has been taught thus, for the awakening of the knowledge of the intelligent.
notes: 'jñānaprabodhāya' can be 'for awakening knowledge' (in the intelligent) or 'for awakening of their knowledge'; the plain rendering is kept.

hindi: जैसे सब वैद्य समझेंगे, वैसे ही उपदेश दिया जाएगा।
english: As, however, all physicians will understand, so it will be taught.
notes: 'bhiṣajaḥ' is run into the previous word in print ('sarvebhiṣajo'), a spacing matter only. 'vijñāsyanti' is read as a future 'will understand'.
